kandidaten.titel: Seed Potato Farm Worker Required 36ph Approx 8 Months Work
kandidaten.beschreibung: We are preparing to start a new seed potato season on our farm. We are seeking a keen individual looking to experience a full seasonal cycle on our farm, casual role, approx. 8 months period (November 2026 to June 2027). Job roles include, but not limited to: - Operating petrol powered counterbalance forklifts - Operating forklifts on tractors - Operating off road forklifts - Operating tractors with mowing and tillage implements - Operating tractors with various other implements - Driving trucks and other work vehicles (on the farm) - Cleaning of work areas - Basic maintenance of machines - Cleaning of machines - In field rogueing of potatoes and possibly a small amount of hand weeding - Working on your own and with a team - Cutting seed potatoes - Grading seed potatoes - Various simple and easy manual labour tasks There is a wide variety of tasks involved in this job, it is not just operating machinery. Please keep this in mind when applying. The role is perfectly suited to both female and male workers, nothing is particularly heavy labour intensive. A typical season looks like this: November - Ground prep and getting ready to plant, tractor work (long hours very busy, approx. 40-60+hrs per week) December - Ground prep, seed preparation, planting seed potatoes (long hours very busy, approx. 40-60+hrs p/w) January - Finish planting, crop care, tractor mowing, crop rogueing, weeding, various simple jobs, some field tractor work. (More flexible hours, e.g. time to go to the beach and enjoy Albany's summer, approx. 20-40hrs p/w. February - Mid season crop care, tractor mowing, crop rogueing, weeding, various simple jobs, preparation for harvest, some field tractor work (More flexible hours, approx. 20-40hrs p/w) March - Build up to start harvest, start harvest, some crop care, various simple jobs, harvest team starts. (Still flexible hours, but building up to peak season again, approx. 20-40hrs p/w) April - Full swing harvest, now with full harvest team, combination of harvesting and grading, possibly some field tractor work, forklift use etc (Approx. 35-50hrs p/w hours, revolves around the harvest team and structured hours) May - Harvest finished, full-time grading and packing, forklift work, possibly some tractor work. (Approx. 35-45hrs p/w, structured hours around harvest team) June - Finishing up grading and packing, after harvest work, general farm tasks. This role is suitable and available to both Domestic workers and Working Holiday Visa holders. We are prepared to tailor the role to suit your personal circumstances where possible. For WHV holders, the job is likely to meet the 6 months work requirement for 2nd year Visa (or 3 months 1st year). As this is an agricultural job, it is exempt from the 6 months single job work limit. Forklift and/or tractor experience preferrable, but not essential. Forklift ticket and/or a heavy rigid driver's licence would be useful, but not essential. The job is located approx. 7 minutes drive from Albany CBD. Typical hours are 7:00am to approx. 5:00pm during planting, approx. 8:00am - 4:00pm during crop care period, 7:00am to 4:00pm during harvest and grading. You will need your own vehicle to get to and from the farm every day, you will need to bring your own food for the day, typically 2 meal breaks per day. For WHV, you will need your own accommodation, we do have basic camping facilities on site (shower/toilet, basic kitchen with fridge and microwave, dry and warm areas to relax in) but you will need your own sleeping arrangement (tent, campervan etc). Camping is provided free to our farm workers. The casual wage will be 36 p/h, the job operates under the national horticulture award MA000028. Applying for the job: - Please send your up-to-date resume/CV detailing your work experience. - Please provide your contact details, including phone number and email. - If you are not currently located in Albany, please advise your current location. - If you are a Visa holder, please specify which

Phillip Island Winery is recruiting casual front-of-house team members now, with roles available as we build towards summer and work continuing through the peak season and into autumn. Spend the season surrounded by Phillip Island’s incredible beaches and coastline, with predominantly daytime hours and plenty to enjoy outside work. At the Winery, you’ll also be joining a pretty special crew. They’re the people who make the place what it is – warm, welcoming, hands-on and always ready to pitch in for each other when things get busy. THE OPPORTUNITIES We have several casual roles available across: • Restaurant service • Bar and beverage service • Cellar door and wine tastings • Weddings and events • General front-of-house support We’re recruiting people with different levels of hospitality experience and will match successful applicants to the work that best suits their skills and interests. Some roles need previous experience. Every role needs the right attitude. WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR We want good humans who are: • Positive, reliable and ready to pitch in • Warm and genuine with guests • Comfortable working as part of a close team • Willing to learn and take feedback • Available across weekends, public holidays and peak summer dates Previous experience in a restaurant, winery, cellar door, bar, café or events environment will be valuable. A current Victorian RSA will be required for roles involving alcohol service. If you don’t yet have one, you must be willing to obtain it before commencing in a relevant role. Working Holiday Makers and travellers with valid Australian working rights are welcome to apply. WHAT THE SEASON LOOKS LIKE • Roles available to commence now and throughout the lead-up to summer • Work continuing through summer and into autumn • At least 10 hours per week, with opportunities for more during peak periods • Hours generally between 10am and 6pm, with some additional or extended hours for weddings and events • Casual rates under the Hospitality Industry (General) Award, including applicable penalty rates • Based at Phillip Island Winery in Ventnor Accommodation isn’t provided, but we can share a current guide to options around Phillip Island and the surrounding area, including hostel or backpacker-style accommodation where available. You will need to be able to travel reliably to and from the Winery for shifts. ABOUT PHILLIP ISLAND WINERY Phillip Island Winery brings together quality wine, seasonal food and relaxed hospitality in a beautiful rural setting. Our guests join us for everything from casual lunches and wine tastings to weddings, events and special celebrations. Behind it all is a close, hard-working crew who care about giving people a genuinely good day at the Winery. APPLY If good hospitality, an amazing crew and a summer on Phillip Island sound like your kind of combination, we’d love to hear from you. Read the full role details and complete our application form at: https://www.phillipislandwinery.com.au/careers

It is a fully furnished house, no charge – except for electricity bills (monthly). We expect the house to be kept tidy and lawns mowed regularly. We ride a 2 wheel motorbike on the farm ( it is quite easy, we can teach you!), and will provide you with waterproof jacket and pants, but you need your own gumboots (a warm beanie is recommended too!). Flytande kunskaper i finska, svenska och engelska i både tal och skrift.

Vana av att arbeta tvärfunktionellt med inköp, marknad och tech.

Söderhamns kommun söker engagerad medarbetare till Skärgårdsenheten
Skärgårdsenheten är en relativt liten enhet bestående av 5 personer. Arbetsuppgifterna är varierande med arbete till sjöss och på land. Teamet ansvarar för underhållsarbeten och reparationer av bryggor och andra byggnader, transporter av sopor från våra miljöstationer ute på öarna in till fastlandet, underhåll av kommunens farleder samt transporter av passagerare till och från våra uthyrningsanläggningar i skärgården. Säkerställa farleder för yrkes- och fritidstrafik, upprätthålla passagerartrafik i skärgården, tillhandahålla och upprätthålla god kvalité på anläggningar för rörligt friluftsliv i skärgården, säkerställa att uthyrningsanläggningar håller god nivå vad gäller renlighet, utrustning och standard.

Att utveckla rutiner och arbetssätt för att hela tiden eftersträva förbättringar är för dig en självklarhet!
Hos oss får du chansen att arbeta i en dynamisk och naturnära miljö, där varje dag bjuder på nya möjligheter att bidra till skärgårdens utveckling och välbefinnande. Bli en del av vårt engagerade team och vara med och skapa oförglömliga upplevelser för alla som besöker Söderhamns skärgård.

Upptäck en unik arbetsmiljö i Söderhamns skärgård!

Vi säkerställer att både fritidstrafik och yrkestrafik kan navigera tryggt och effektivt till våra allmänna hamnar i Stugsund, Långrör och Orrskär.

Körkort B manuell -Svenska och engelska i tal oc

kandidaten.beschreibung:
Stibyggjaren AS søker etter spesielt kvalifiserte steinarbeidere til fysisk og mentalt krevende arbeid ute i fjellet gjennom sammenhengende 6 måneder i sesongen 2026. Alle arbeider utføres manuelt med klassisk håndverktøy (spett, slegge, steinhammer, meisel, fyllhakke og bøtte).

 Hva vi ser etter

 Vi ser etter kompetanse og viktige, personlige egenskaper: 

 Kjernekompetanse og utfyllende kompetansekrav: 

 6 år erfaring i naturstein-/gråsteinsmuring hvorav erfaring fra rehabilitering av historisk murverk tillegges avgjørende vekt.

 Gjennom erfaring tilegnet høy sosial kompetanse i arbeidssituasjon.

 Gjennom erfaring tilegnet god kjennskap til egen fysiske - og ikke minst viktig; mental styrke og svakhet.

 Solid erfaring i å "lese" naturstein for effektivt å splitte eller tilhugge.

 Erfaring fra prosessuell restaurering av bakkemurer og gråsteinsmurer i gamle, bevaringsverdige/vernede bygninger.

 Evne og vilje til trygg og god kommunikasjon med team-kolleger/ arbeidsleder på norsk og engelsk er påkrevet.

 Positiv innstilling til arbeidet også under krevende vær og arbeidsforhold.

 God kunnskap, evner og vilje i å ivareta helse, sikkerhet og et trygt og på alle måter godt arbeidsmiljø for absolutt alle på laget.

 Arbeidsoppgaver

 Arbeidet omfatter grovt sett to kategorier oppdrag hvorav klassisk steinarbeid på stier i bratt/krevende terreng er svært viktig. Like viktig denne sesongen er oppdrag av type klassisk gråsteinsarbeid på vegmurer, husmurer bakkemurer mv. - mest oppdrag av type restaurering/rehabilitering. Søker må beherske begge kategorier arbeid. Merk også at vi snakker utelukkende om faget tørrmuring - gråsteinsmuring uten mørtel/bindemiddel av noe slag.

 Alle oppdrag skal løses ved fullt ut manuelt steinarbeid med klassisk håndverktøy (slegge, meisel, steinhammer, spett, fyllhakke og bøtte).

 Vi tilbyr

 Vi tilbyr 6 måneders ansettelse for dem som med sikkerhet vet at de vil klare å trives og gjøre godt arbeid i et fast sammensatt firemanns arbeidslag gjennom hele sesongen.

 Vi tilbyr timelønn etter avtale og øvrige arbeidsvilkår i hht. norske regler.

kandidaten.beschreibung:
Om stillingen
 Ved Institutt for farmasi (IFA), Det helsevitenskapelige fakultet er det en ledig stilling som stipendiat tilknyttet forskningsgruppen cellesignalisering og målrettet terapi . Stillingen er tilknyttet prosjektet «Utvikling av nye strategier for behandling av terapiresistent blodkreft basert på proximity-indusert farmakologi».
 Stillingen gjelder for en periode på fire år. Ph.d.-studiet er normert til tre år. Det fjerde året, fordelt med 25 % pr år, skal brukes til undervisning eller andre karrierefremmende arbeidsoppgaver etter avtale . Stipendiatstillingen er en utdanningsstilling og har fullført forskerutdanning frem til doktorgrad som mål. Opptak til doktorgradsprogram er en forutsetning for ansettelse og studieperioden starter ved tiltredelse i stillingen.
 Arbeidssted er UiT i Tromsø. Du må kunne starte i stillingen innen rimelig tid etter å ha mottatt tilbud.

 Om prosjektet
 I prosjektet vil vi utforske proximity-farmakologi som en ny terapeutisk strategi innen kreftbehandling. Tilnærmingen bygger på små molekyler eller bifunksjonelle forbindelser som bringer to eller flere proteiner i fysisk nærhet for å fremkalle en definert biologisk respons. I motsetning til tradisjonelle legemidler, som vanligvis hemmer eller aktiverer ett enkelt protein gjennom direkte binding, kan proximity-farmakologi omprogrammere proteininteraksjoner og signalnettverk på en mer dynamisk måte.
 Vi vil bruke denne strategien til å påvirke signalveier som regulerer programmert celledød i kreftceller. Slike signalveier er sentrale for effekten av kreftbehandling, men er ofte forstyrret i behandlingsresistent sykdom og ved tilbakefall. Prosjektet skal derfor undersøke hvordan proximity-baserte forbindelser kan brukes til å gjenopprette eller forsterke kreftcellenes evne til å gjennomgå målrettet celledød, med mål om å identifisere nye behandlingsprinsipper for terapirefraktær kreft.
 Ph.d.-prosjektet er forankret i et nasjonalt og internasjonalt samarbeid mellom Institutt for farmasi ved UiT Norges arktiske universitet, University Hospital Schleswig-Holstein i Kiel, K.G. Jebsen-senter for myeloid blodkreft ved Universitetet i Bergen og Haukeland universitetssjukehus, Institutt for kreftforskning ved Oslo universitetssykehus og MRC Phosphorylation and Ubiquitinylation Unit ved University of Dundee. Samarbeidet samler komplementær kompetanse innen farmakologi, kreftbiologi, hematologisk kreft, proteinkinase- og fosfataseregulering samt proximity-baserte legemiddelstrategier. Dette gir et solid faglig og teknologisk grunnlag for å utvikle innovative tilnærminger som kan utløse selektiv celledød i kreftceller.

 Kvalifikasjoner
 For stillingen kreves mastergrad eller tilsvarende i molekylærvitenskap, molekylærbiologi, cellebiologi, biokjemi, bioteknologi,  farmasi eller lignende. Det kreves også erfaring fra eksperimentelt laboratoriearbeid. Kandidaten må har erfaring med en eller flere av disse teknikkene:
 Rekombinante DNA teknikker, inkludert primerdesign, kloning og vektorkonstruksjon
 Proteinkjemi inkludert uttrykk og karakterisering av proteiner 
 Molekylær cellebiologi inkludert dyrkning av celler, transfeksjon, mikroskopi, immunofarging og Western-blotting.
 Ettersom 25% av stillingen er avsatt til undervisning, vil dokumentert undervisningserfaring, gjerne med relevans til farmakologi, bli vektlagt positivt. Erfaring med og/eller gjennomført kurs i bioinformatikk vil også telle positivt.
 Søkere skal ha dokumentert gode kunnskaper i engelsk, og kunne jobbe i et internasjonalt miljø. Nordiske søkere kan dokumentere dette med vitnemål fra videregående skole. Søkere må også ha dokumentert gode kunnskaper i norsk (eller annet skandinavisk språk).
 I bedømmelsen vektlegges søkerens potensial for å gjennomføre en forskerutdanning basert på masteroppgaven eller tilsvarende, og eventuelle andre vitenskapelige arbeider. I tillegg vil det tas hensyn til yrkespraksis og annen erfaring av betydning for gjennomføring av doktorgradsstudiet.

kandidaten.beschreibung:
Om stillingen
 Ved Institutt for farmasi (IFA), Det helsevitenskapelige fakultet er det en ledig stilling som stipendiat tilknyttet forskningsgruppe for klinisk farmasi og farmakoepidemiologi (IPSUM).
 Stillingen gjelder for en periode på tre år. Stipendiatstillingen er en utdanningsstilling og har fullført forskerutdanning frem til doktorgrad som mål. Opptak til doktorgradsprogram er en forutsetning for ansettelse og studieperioden starter ved tiltredelse i stillingen.
 Arbeidssted er UiT i Tromsø. Du må kunne starte i stillingen innen rimelig tid etter å ha mottatt tilbud.

 Om prosjektet
 Stillingen er tilknyttet prosjektet « Bruk av Tromsøundersøkelsesdata for fremme av apotekfarmasi ». Prosjektets hovedmål er å bidra til bedre legemiddelbehandling i både individ og samfunnsperspektiv.  Som del av dette skal prosjektet skal denne PhDen se på følgende problemstillinger:
 1. Fornøydhet med legemiddelinformasjon i apotek 
 Hvilke faktorer beskriver deltakere som er enten fornøyd eller misfornøyd med informasjonen de mottar om sine legemidler i apotek? (f.eks. demografi, legemiddelgrupper, mottak av inhalasjonsveiledning eller medisinstart). Er det sammenheng mellom fornøydhet og mottak av informasjon fra apotek og fastlege, med generelle holdninger til legemidler eller med oppnåelse av terapimål? Hvis det kan undersøkes, er det en sammenheng med mottak av apotektjenester som Medisinstart eller Inhalasjonsveiledning? 
 2. Viktighet av legemidler 
 Er det overensstemmelse mellom hva legemiddelbrukerne mener er deres aller viktigste legemiddel og hva helsepersonell (farmasøyter) mener er det viktigste? Hva kjennetegner eventuelt deltakere med uoverensstemmelse på dette punktet? Er det sammenheng mellom uoverensstemmelser og faktorer som holdninger til legemidler eller oppnåelse av terapimål?  
 3. Synspunkter og holdninger til legemiddelbruk 
 Hvilke generelle synspunkter og holdninger til legemidler har legemiddelbrukere i en generell norsk befolkning? Hvilke faktorer beskriver de ulike kategorier av synspunkter og holdninger?
 Data fra  Tromsøundersøkelsen , med kobling til  Legemiddelregisteret , gir mulighet til å identifisere viktige målgrupper for slike tjenester. Studiepopulasjonen vil inkludere deltakere i Tromsøundersøkelsen som rapporterer legemiddelbruk (ca. 10 000) og data vil blant annet inkludere om man har mottatt legemiddelinformasjon fra lege og/eller apotek, informasjonsbehov, synspunkter og holdninger til legemidler og legemiddelbruk, i tillegg til hvilke legemidler man bruker og andre relevante variabler på helse, livsstil og sosiodemografi. Se  helsedata.no for oversikt over variabler i Tromsøundersøkelsen og Legemiddelregisteret.
 Søkerne må levere en kort prosjektbeskrivelse (maks 800 ord pluss eventuelle referanser) av det faglige grunnlaget, potensielle forskningsspørsmål og foreslått metode og argumenter for metodevalg for doktorgradsprosjektet ved innsending av søknad. Den endelige prosjektbeskrivelsen vil bli utviklet i samarbeid med veilederne.

 Kvalifikasjoner
 For stillingen kreves mastergrad eller tilsvarende i farmasi, andre helsefag, helseinformatikk eller lignende. Masteroppgaven må være innen samfunnsfarmasi, farmakoepidemiologi, epidemiologi eller informatikk med bruk av helsedata. Relevant Forskningserfaring utover masteroppgaven er en fordel, men ikke et krav.
 Søkere skal dokumentere gode kunnskaper i engelsk. Nordiske søkere kan dokumentere dette med vitnemål fra videregående skole. 
 I bedømmelsen vektlegges søkerens potensial for å gjennomføre en forskerutdanning basert på masteroppgaven, eventuell annen forskningserfaring og prosjektbeskrivelsen (se over). Det vil også tas hensyn til annen erfaring av betydning for gjennomføring av doktorgradsstudiet, for eksempel erfaring/jobb i felt som genererer data som skal brukes, slik som helsevesenet inkludert apotek .

kandidaten.titel: Ph.D. Candidate in Reinforcement Learning for Project Scheduling Problems
kandidaten.organisation: NTNU - Norwegian University of Science and Technology
kandidaten.beschreibung:
This is NTNU
 NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.
 At NTNU, 9,000 employees and 43,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.
 You will find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here. 

Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41s About the position
 Are you motivated to take a step towards a doctorate and open up exciting career opportunities? As a PhD Candidate with us, you will work to achieve your doctorate, and at the same time gain valuable experience that qualifies you for a further career in higher education and research, in and outside academia.
 The position will specifically focus on Reinforcement Learning for Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling Problem (RCPSP). The Ph.D. candidate will be a member of the group of Civil Engineering and Geomatics at NTNU and will tightly cooperate with other Ph.D./post-docs in projects (such as HEU-CIRCULess) and research groups at the department. The Ph.D. position will offer opportunities to develop high-quality research within the field of digitalization of circular construction.
 Your immediate leader will be the Head of Department.

 Duties of the position

 Develop learning-based algorithms or methods for deterministic scheduling optimization problems with the aim of achieving competitive performance against state-of-the-art approaches. 
 Extend the developed framework to scheduling under uncertainty. Investigate how the proposed learning-based methods can be extended to uncertain and dynamic project environments.
 Improve the scalability of learning-based scheduling methods and evaluate generalization, robustness, and computational performance.
 Disseminate research outcomes. Publications in relevant high quality peer-reviewed journals  are needed. 
 Complete the doctoral education until obtaining a doctorate
 Carry out research of good quality within the framework described above
 Academic publications and popular science dissemination
 Participate in the research group  Civil Engineering and Geomatics Research group Civil Engineering and Geomatics - NTNU 
 Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment.

 Required selection criteria
 You must have a relevant master’s degree in Computer Science and technology, computer system engineering or equivalent. Your course of study must correspond to a five-year Norwegian course, where 120 credits have been obtained at master's level. 
 Experience in reinforcement learning, GNN, etc.
 You must have a strong academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your Master's degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to  NTNU's grading scale . If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker grade background, you may be considered if you can document that you are particularly suitable for a PhD education.
 You must meet the requirements for admission to the faculty's Doctoral Programme  https://www.ntnu.edu/studies/phiv 
 Applicants must have fluent skills in both written and oral English. Non-English native speaker applicants who do not have master in Europe must provide evidence of good English language skills, written and spoken. The following tests can be used as such documentation: TOEFL, IELTS or Cambridge Certificate in Advanced English (CAE) or Cambridge Certificate of Proficiency in English (CPE). Minimum scores are: TOEFL: 600 (paper-based test), 92 (Internet-based test); IELTS: 6.5, with no section lower than 5.5 (only Academic IELTS test accepted); CAE/CPE: grade B or A.
  In extraordinary circumstances, formal documentation of language skills can be relinquished. In such cases, the candidate’s language skills will be assessed in a personal interview.

 PLEASE NOTE: For d

kandidaten.beschreibung:
Kunnskap som formar samfunnet
 UiB skal vere blant Europas fremste universitet, internasjonalt kjent for høg kvalitet i forsking og utdanning. Som samfunnsinstitusjon skal vi bidra til ei berekraftig og demokratisk utvikling og vere ein attraktiv og inkluderande studie- og arbeidsplass.
Video: https://youtu.be/M5n6RnScNgA Postdoktorstilling 
 Ved  Michael Sars-senteret  er det ledig ei stilling som postdoktor i mekanismar for temperaturrobustheit hos fiskeembryo i  Čapek-gruppa . Stillinga er for ein åremålsperiode på tre år og er finansiert av Universitetet i Bergen.

 Om prosjektet/arbeidsoppgåver:
 Korleis kan fiskeembryo oppretthalde koordinert utvikling når temperaturendringar påverkar farten på molekylære og cellulære prosessar? Forskinga vår undersøkjer mekanismane som gjer embryoutvikling robust mot temperaturvariasjonar, og under kva forhold denne robustheita bryt saman. Vi kombinerer etablerte fiskemodellar med marine fiskeartar for å forstå korleis embryo frå ulike termiske miljø reagerer på temperaturendringar.
 Den tilsette skal undersøkje korleis temperatur påverkar utviklingsregulerande signalvegar og genuttrykk, og korleis desse responsane heng saman med spesifisering av cellelagnad, vevsorganisering og embryoutvikling. Arbeidet vil kombinere transkriptomiske eksperiment og bioinformatiske analysar med molekylære analysar, genomredigering og mikroskopi av levande og fikserte embryo. Eit sentralt mål er å knyte transkripsjonelle responsar til utviklingsmessige utfall og funksjonelt teste kandidatmekanismar for temperaturrobustheit.
 I tett samarbeid med gruppeleiar og andre medlemmer av forskingsgruppa skal den tilsette utvikle eit sjølvstendig forskingsprosjekt innanfor denne ramma, basert på eiga fagleg kompetanse, vitskaplege interesser og eigne idéar.

 Kvalifikasjonar og eigenskapar:
 Søkjarar må ha oppnådd ein grad tilsvarande ein norsk doktorgrad (ph.d.) innanfor utviklingsbiologi, molekylærbiologi, marinbiologi eller eit nærliggande fagområde, eller ha levert doktoravhandlinga si til vurdering innan søknadsfristen er ute. Det er ein føresetnad at doktorgraden er oppnådd før tilsetjing kan skje             
 Dokumentert forskingserfaring innan transkriptomikk, inkludert forsøksdesign, praktisk gjennomføring av eksperiment, bioinformatiske analysar og biologisk tolking av dei innsamla dataa, er eit krav
 Dokumentert forskingserfaring innan eksperimentell utviklingsbiologi er eit krav. Relevante metodar omfattar til dømes mikroinjeksjon, immunfarging, CRISPR-Cas9-basert genomredigering og mikroskopi av levande og fikserte prøvar. Det er ikkje krav om erfaring med alle desse metodane
 Forskingserfaring med fisk og/eller marine organismar er ein fordel
 Forskingserfaring innan evolusjonær utviklingsbiologi, komparativ utviklingsbiologi eller utviklingsresponsar på miljøvariasjonar, inkludert temperatur, er ein fordel
 Søkjarar må kunne arbeide sjølvstendig, strukturert og ha gode samarbeidsevner
 Søkjarar må ha gode engelskkunnskapar, skriftleg og munnleg
 Personlege og mellommenneskelege eigenskapar vil bli lagt vekt på. Forskingserfaring, ambisjonar og potensial vil også telle ved vurdering av kandidatane.
 Særeigne krav for stillinga 
UiB er underlagd regelverket for eksportkontroll og regelverket gjeld ved behandling av søknadar til stillinga.

 Om postdoktorstillinga:
 Postdoktorstillinga er ei åremålsstilling og har som hovudmål å kvalifisere den som blir tilsett for arbeid i vitskaplege toppstillingar. Kandidatar som manglar undervisningserfaring og/eller annan kvalifiseringskompetanse, vil få høve til kvalifiserande arbeid, anten i åremålsperioden eller gjennom eventuell forlenging av åremålsperioden (maks fire år totalt). Stillinga vil kunne bli forlenga med inntil eitt år dersom kandidaten får innvilga forskingsopphald i utlandet frå eksterne kjelder (maks fire år totalt). kandidaten.beschreibung:
Location: Toucan Ridge Ecology and Education Society  Open Period: Open on a rolling basis. Duration: Sessions may be 2 to 5 weeks, with 4 weeks recommended for maximum learning  Hours per Week: 35 – 40  Cost: $289USD/Week    Description:     Internships take place at the T.R.E.E.S Hosting Center, a research and education facility in the Maya Mountains of Belize. The center is operated by the Toucan Ridge Ecology and Education Society (T.R.E.E.S), a small grassroots nonprofit dedicated to conserving Belize’s natural and cultural heritage through education, conservation, and research. One way we fulfill this mission is by hosting interns. Through training international and local Belizean students in environmental and wildlife management, field research techniques, and data collection protocols, we contribute to a greater understanding of Belize’s biodiversity.      At T.R.E.E.S, the only resident turtle species is the White-lipped Mud Turtle (Kinosternon leucostomum). This internship focuses on using radio telemetry to study the movements and habitat preferences of individual Mud Turtles. We have equipped nine turtles with transmitters, and the intern will track them daily. Recently, T.R.E.E.S documented a Furrowed Wood Turtle (Rhinoclemmys areolata) on the property, the first record of this species in the area. Since this species is typically found in tropical savanna habitats, its presence here is unusual. Two volunteer/intern field assistant positions are available 20 Feb to 15 Jun 2027 , to take part in an ongoing behavioral study of female mate choice and male display behavior in Lance- tailed Manakins ( Chiroxiphia lanceolata ) in Panama. These positions are designed to maximize training opportunities for post-graduate students who are seeking experience in basic science research as they consider applying to graduate school.

 Research background: Females of this small, lekking bird “shop” among males that display in cooperative pairs on dispersed display areas. Successful applicants will be involved in work investigating how strong sexual selection is changing this wild population over time, how male experience affects display performance and cooperative behavior, why dominant males tolerate subordinate cooperators, and how indirect genetic benefits affect female mate choice and maternal investment.

The full field crew is a 4-5 person team of researchers who will live and work on a remote island off of Panama's Pacific coast and share housing with close quarters. The site provides internet access and cell phone reception, but unpredictable power outages can happen and last for days. In addition to the usual need for experience working in isolated field settings and/or shared living situations with little privacy, applicants should be level-headed, resilient, and responsible to work safely and thrive during their time with this project. Team members should be comfortable engaging respectfully with the local community, including through our annual outreach day at the local primary school.

 This is a demanding six-day-per-week field position; in addition to scheduled data collection (approximately 30 hours/week), it also entails long hot hikes to reach data collection sites,  data entry and organization requirements, and shared household responsibilities that require daily effort, making this a full-time commitment while in the field. Applicants should be enthusiastic, physically fit, and emotionally grounded. Expect to work long days, be woken at 4 am by howler monkeys on a regular basis, and see some amazing bird behavior. A sense of humor, ability to work independently, and willingness to accommodate unpredictable changes is especially important. Conversational Spanish ability is strongly preferred for this position. Assistants are also required to complete online animal care and use training shortly after being hired.

 Compensation: Food, housing, and required transportation within Panama will be provided, as well as a $1500 honorarium upon completion of the field season to help defray costs of health insurance and personal purchases. Assistants will also be reimbursed for round-trip airfare to Panama City, Panama (up to $750) upon completion of the field season, and will need to provide their own snake gaiters (~$50) and to follow any Covid testing/vaccination requirements for travel. Species recorded include the African Fish Eagle, European Bee-eater, Little Bee-eater, Martial Eagle, Saddle-billed Stork, Woolly-necked Stork, African Spoonbill, African Openbill, Little Grebe, Knob-billed Duck, and Lesser Moorhen. 
 Regular bird surveys are conducted across different habitat types to document species presence, abundance, and distribution. Bird data collected through the project are also shared with other research organisations in South Africa.

kandidaten.titel: PhD position: road impacts on species of conservation concern
kandidaten.beschreibung:
Description  

 The Holmes lab at Southern Illinois University is recruiting a PhD student for a fully funded, 5-year research assistantship. Application deadline is December 30. Salary is $25,700 per year. The research should focus on the impacts of roads on natural systems in the eastern hardwood forest, ideally with the possibility of improving conservation practices for state and federal threatened and endangered species. Contact Iris Holmes ( iris.holmes@siu.edu ) for more information. 

 Duties  

 The student will conduct sampling for threatened and endangered bats at new construction sites (approximately 5-10 per year). Sampling will involve laying out tarps to collect fecal samples, preserving samples in the field, extracting DNA from the samples in the lab, and using Sanger sequencing to barcode the samples to identify bat species. A report on species IDs must be completed within 15 days of sample collection. 

 Research focus  

 In addition to bat monitoring, the student will develop a research program as part of the new Roadside Ecology Center at SIU. The taxon focus is flexible, but the research should apply to conservation of threatened and endangered species or to conservation of Illinois habitats. Possible research areas could include (but are not limited to) validating eDNA methods for detection of vertebrates or invertebrates from water samples, using eDNA methods to study connectivity in aquatic systems, developing analytical methods to account for imperfect detection in metapopulation or niche models, quantifying road impacts on animal diets, or determining the impact of construction- or road-related stressors on animal microbiomes or parasite infection rates. 

 Desired qualifications  

 Bachelor’s degree in biology or a related field 

 Master’s degree or 1 or more years of work experience 

 Experience with molecular lab work and/or field work 

 Interest in landscape management or conservation policy

kandidaten.beschreibung:
Antioch University is offering partial scholarships and work study positions, if you enroll in the Environmental Studies Master’s program, and is accepting applications to start your MS degree during the spring semester of 2027. MS Concentrations include Conservation Biology, Environmental Education, and Advocacy for Social Justice and Sustainability. In Conservation Biology, students focus on gaining quantitative (GIS and statistics), writing, and ecological field skills. Students also gain experience with community engagement, social justice, and applied research and service. 

 Students can earn their graduate degree with either face-to-face classes at the Antioch University New England campus in Keene, NH, USA, or fully online classes (that can be taken from anywhere) which are offered each semester, or with a mixture of the two. Ecological field trip classes (intensive 1-2 week trips to destinations abroad and in-country) are also available for all students. All classes are just 1-2 days a week, making this a viable program for environmental professionals working part or full-time. Our programs are student-centered, flexible, and tailored to meet your individual needs, learning style, and location.

 Students often work with Antioch faculty in our existing research programs. Specifically in our Conservation Biology concentration, we have expertise in vertebrate ecology (e.g., birds, snakes), invertebrate ecology (e.g., estuarine invertebrates, insects), tropical ecology, forest ecology, alpine ecology, marine ecology, and coastal restoration. In some cases, faculty may have extramural funding to support students in seasonal field and lab positions, including research in New England and in the Caribbean. Students who are eligible for US federal work-study can also work part time in various on-campus work-study positions, including Graduate Teaching and Research Assistantships and various positions in our numerous campus centers (e.g., Institute for International Conservation, Spatial Analysis Lab). However, you need to be accepted and taking classes as a graduate student to be eligible for these work-study positions. Students at Antioch generally pay for at least part of their own tuition, but we offer numerous university-wide grants and scholarships, which can help defray tuition costs, and which are detailed here: https://www.antioch.edu/admission-aid/financial-aid/scholarships-and-grants/ . We also work with students to help them apply for external scholarships, fellowships, and research-focused grants.

 Join our tight-knit community as we strive to advance social and environmental justice, conserve biodiversity, and mitigate climate change as a department and as a university! For more information about our programs, visit our webpages ( https://www.antioch.edu/academics/program-finder?_sft_focus=environmental-studies-sustainability ,  https://www.antioch.edu/academics/environmental-studies-sustainability/environmental-studies-ms/conservation-biology-es-ms/ ) or contact Melissa Baptiste, Admissions Counselor, at mbaptiste (at) antioch.edu .

kandidaten.beschreibung:
The Holbrook Team and Colorado Parks and Wildlife (CPW) are recruiting a Research Scientist to join them at the University of Wyoming (work location will be in Laramie, WY). The Research Scientist will primarily be working at the intersection of elk behavioral ecology and human recreation. We have deployed an extensive network of trail counters and cameras, as well as GPS units to recreationists, to sample human recreation. We have also acquired privatized human mobility data to add to our sample of humans recreating on our landscapes of interest.  Additionally, over the last 6 years, our team has deployed GPS collars on 280 adult female elk in the two main study locations. The main objective for this position is to advance our understanding regarding human-elk interactions, and provide guidance on recreation development into the future. Recreation is multi-billion dollar economy, and generating insights that inform the development conversation for wildlife conservation is really our hope with this position.  
See the following webpages for more information on the Holbrook Team (https://sites.google.com/site/josephdholbrook03/) at the University of Wyoming.  
Candidates should have expertise in a suite of modeling approaches aimed at understanding animal-habitat relationships and animal movement.  Candidates should show creativity and flexible thinking, be extremely self-motivated, and have an authentic desire to cultivate real-world insights from data analyses. Candidates should also be able to work exceptionally well with a team of collaborators.  
The position is for one to three years , with appointment for the second year and beyond contingent on performance and project funding. Financial support for travel to attend at least one conference will also be available.

 Develop skills in data quality assurance, documentation, and standardized management of research-program information.

The Wisely Lab in the University of Florida Department of Wildlife Ecology and Conservation is recruiting a Ph.D. student to join a multidisciplinary project developing innovative approaches for surveillance of feral swine and African swine fever virus (ASFV).

 The project uses mosquito bloodmeals as biological samples of free-ranging feral swine , an approach known as exogenous xenosurveillance. By treating blood-fed mosquitoes as “flying syringes,” the research team will evaluate whether mosquito bloodmeals can be used to detect feral swine, genetically identify individual animals, estimate population abundance, and support pathogen surveillance.

Position responsibilities

 The Ph.D. student will take a leading role in the field ecology and quantitative components of the project. Responsibilities will include:

 ·         Coordinating deployment and sampling of camera traps and mosquito capture systems across wet and dry seasons.

 ·         Supervising and mentoring undergraduate researchers participating in field and laboratory activities.

 ·         Working with project collaborators to process mosquito bloodmeals and generate genetic data for individual identification of feral swine.

 ·         Developing genetic mark-recapture models to estimate feral swine abundance from mosquito-derived host DNA.

 ·         AND/OR

 ·         Developing occupancy/detection models to compare the effectiveness of mosquito-based surveillance and conventional camera trapping.

 The student will be co-advised by Dr. Samantha Wisely, a wildlife disease ecologist in UF's Department of Wildlife Ecology and Conservation, and Dr. Nathan Burkett-Cadena , a vector-borne disease ecologist at the UF Florida Medical Entomology Laboratory. The student will also collaborate closely with Dr. Tim Smyser of the USDA APHIS Wildlife Services National Feral Swine Damage Management Program on genomic approaches for individual identification of feral swine. The student will have the opportunity to also interact with Dr. Amy Vittor from the College of Medicine on serological assay development. 

 An important feature of the project is the integration of research with agricultural biosecurity education. The successful candidate will work closely with a Ph.D. student specializing in science communication/agricultural education , sharing field experiences, data and scientific expertise that will inform educational materials, microcredentials and a graduate learning module in genetic mark-recapture. The science communications Ph.D. student, mentored by Dr. Grady Roberts , will lead development of the educational products; this position will contribute scientific content and collaborate on their development but will not lead the project's education component.

Minimum qualifications

 Applicants should have:

 ·         A bachelor's or master's degree in wildlife ecology, ecology, entomology, biology, quantitative ecology, disease ecology, or a related field .

 ·         Previous experience conducting ecological field research.

 ·         Demonstrated interest in wildlife population ecology, wildlife disease, quantitative ecology, or wildlife surveillance .

 ·         Experience with, or strong interest in learning, population modeling and statistical analysis in R .

 ·         Ability and willingness to conduct extended fieldwork under hot, humid and physically demanding Florida conditions.

 ·         Strong organizational, written communication and teamwork skills.

 ·         Ability to work independently while contributing effectively to a highly interdisciplinary research team.

 Experience with camera trapping, mosquito or other arthropod sampling, molecular ecology/genetics, occupancy modeling, capture-recapture analysis, or supervision of field crews is desirable but not required.

Research environment

 The student will join a collaborative team spanning wildlife disease ecology, entomology, genomics, infectious disease and agricultural education

Environmental drivers and spatial prediction of waterfowl breeding abundance, distribution, and population dynamics in the Prairie Pothole Region

 Opportunity : Ph.D. Graduate Research Assistantship 

 Program : Department of Forestry and Environmental Conservation | Clemson University

 Location : Georgetown, SC (James C. Kennedy Waterfowl and Wetlands Conservation Center) and/or Clemson, SC (Clemson’s main campus). The location is flexible and depends on the needs of the student and project. 

 Start Date : Spring 2027 (January) 

 Last Date to Apply : September 30 or open until filled

 General Description : A Ph.D. graduate research assistantship is available through the James C. Kennedy Waterfowl and Wetlands Conservation Center, Clemson University, beginning January 2027 (flexible). This position will support a collaborative research project with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service’s Region 6 & 3 Habitat and Population Evaluation Team (HAPET) to evaluate, refine, and expand spatially explicit models of breeding duck pair abundance, distribution, and recruitment across the U.S. Prairie Pothole Region (USPPR), the Northern Great Plains, and beyond. 

 Background : The USPPR supports 30–50% of North America’s breeding duck populations annually. The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service has collected long-term monitoring data of breeding duck abundance and remotely-sensed wetland habitat information through the Four-Square-Mile Breeding Waterfowl Survey (FSMS) for nearly 40 years. These data are used in spatially explicit models (i.e., decision-support tools) to prioritize where and what type of wetlands and grassland conservation efforts should occur within the USPPR. Amid ongoing efforts to modernize the FSMS and derived decision-support tools, HAPET scientists recently developed new models of breeding duck abundance and recruitment; however, these models must be rigorously evaluated, tested, and expanded to new geographies and across different species before they can be operationalized. Thus, this work has the potential to directly inform conservation and policy decisions for breeding waterfowl in the most important landscape in the Northern Hemisphere. kandidaten.beschreibung:
COURSE DESCRIPTION:  It’s never been more important for scientists to get out of the ivory tower and engage with the public. Social media (“Web 2.0”) tools make it easier than ever before in human history for an expert to share their expertise and passion with the masses, and can offer many other professional benefits to scientists and environmental advocates when used properly. However, far too many well-intentioned scientists and environmental advocates don’t learn how to master these tools, resulting in well-intentioned shouting into the void with no possibility of making positive change. This class will cover online public science engagement, from the basics to advanced tips, tricks, and strategies. It will include a thorough overview of the social media landscape, highlighting the best platforms for different goals, who to follow and how to find them, and how to craft messages. It will include a discussion on public-facing scientific writing and blogs, and a discussion on building social media campaigns with actionable and measurable goals. Case studies of successful (and unsuccessful) social media outreach will be discussed throughout, and there will be many interactive guided activities. Your instructor Dr. David Shiffman is one of the most-followed scientists on social media and has taught masterclasses in online public science engagement to over 1,500 early career scientists on five continents. 
  This is a 1-credit equivalent academic course (16 contact hrs + additional work) where you learn at your own pace over 3 months.   This online course is offered October 14-January 5 in Standard and Premium course formats.     Be sure to inquire about early bird savings of $75 before your desired term!
